raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` with EAGLE3 and a reduced draft vocabulary (e.g. `draft_vocab_size=32000`, `target_vocab_size=128256`) currently refuses to start:

```
ValueError: --speculative-use-rejection-sampling requires the draft and target to
share one vocab, but the draft vocab (32000) != target vocab (128256).
```

The FIXME above that check says *"support reduced (hot) draft vocab by scattering draft probs into the target vocab via the d2t map before the sampling kernel"*:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e33cd0c3a10474c7a0f6efeb69ce2cf4b7a55021/python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py#L264-L278

This PR implements exactly that. Since #42297, `--speculative-use-block-verification` also turns rejection sampling on for EAGLE / EAGLE3, so an EAGLE3 draft with a reduced vocabulary hits this error under block verification without the rejection-sampling flag:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e33cd0c3a10474c7a0f6efeb69ce2cf4b7a55021/python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/speculative_hook.py#L178-L198

### Why it matters for correctness

Without this, an EAGLE3 deployment with a reduced-vocab draft cannot use rejection sampling and runs the target-only tree verifier (`rejected_probs=zeros`), which never consumes the actual draft distribution `q`. How much rejection sampling gains over that verifier depends on the draft/target pair and on the entropy of the workload. We measured three internal pairs, each with a 32K hot-vocab EAGLE3 draft built on an MTP layer and run with 7 draft steps, at target T=1 / draft T=1 with top-k and top-p off, on 14 public benchmarks (gsm8k, math500, aime25, humaneval, mbpp, livecodebench, swe-bench, arena-hard, alpaca, mt-bench, translation, summarization, rag, qa), averaged over concurrency 1/4/8/16:

| draft | mean accept-length gain | per-benchmark range |
|---|---|---|
| cold-start draft, target A | +27% | +15% to +40% |
| draft warm-started from target A's MTP layer | +33% | +21% to +46% |
| draft warm-started from target B's MTP layer, on target B | +13% | +3% to +21% |

The gain tracks target entropy. On target A, per-token predictive entropy at T=1 runs from 0.23 nats (humaneval) to 1.17 nats (qa). The two lowest-entropy sets, humaneval and mbpp, gave the smallest gains in all three pairs (+3% to +24%), and open-ended chat (mt-bench, alpaca, qa) the largest. The Spearman correlation between a benchmark's entropy on target A and its gain is 0.57, 0.76 and 0.90 for the three pairs.

A test on a public pair in the comments ([Qwen3-30B-A3B with a 32K EAGLE3 draft, 3 draft steps](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40893#issuecomment-6608282634)) found the opposite sign: rejection sampling accepted about 4-5% fewer tokens than the target-only verifier there. A lower-entropy workload, a weaker draft (accept length about 1.7 there) and fewer draft steps each shrink the gain. So this flag is a correctness fix that lets the draft distribution count, not a guaranteed speedup.

A two-sample G-test on token-frequency histograms, with a second independent non-speculative launch as the noise floor, finds the new path indistinguishable from that floor, while the `rejected_probs=zeros` path is biased (pooled p = 3.2e-26).

**Where these numbers come from.** They were measured on an older internal fork, with a d2t scatter that is mathematically the same as this PR's but applied at each producer instead of once at the verify boundary. They show what rejection sampling with a scattered `q` does to acceptance and that it stays unbiased. The code in this PR has not been benchmarked end to end; the e2e test below is its first end-to-end check on main.

## Modifications

`spec_utils.py` - add `scatter_draft_probs_to_target_vocab()`:
- `index_copy_` the hot-vocab `q` into a target-vocab-width zero tensor. This is exact, not an approximation: the draft can only ever propose a hot token, so `q(x) = 0` off the hot set is the true proposal mass, and `relu(p - q)` keeps the full `p` there.
- Force fp32 so the eager and CUDA-graph paths hand the kernel the same dtype.
- No buffer reuse: the returned tensor outlives the call under overlap scheduling, so a cached buffer would alias across iterations.

`eagle_worker_v2.py`:
- Replace the FIXME `raise ValueError` with an info log.
- Add `_build_verify_draft_probs()`, which stacks the per-step `q` and scatters once at the kernel boundary rather than in each producer.
- Add `EagleDraftWorker.draft_probs_vocab_size`. Until the verify boundary `q` stays at the draft width, so every buffer that carries it between steps has to be that wide. The idle stub now uses it instead of the target vocab size.
- Under `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT`, assert `q > 0` at every proposed token. A `q` scattered so that a proposed token lands off its support reads back as `q == 0`, which makes the `coin * q < p` accept test vacuously true: accept length pins to `num_steps` while the text silently degrades. Rows with no mass are skipped, because they are CUDA-graph filler: capture warms up on the zeroed `q` buffer, and replay zeroes padded rows. The gather is gated so it never runs in production.
- On a PD-disaggregation decode server, reject a reduced draft vocabulary under rejection sampling at startup. `pd_first_draft_proposal` builds a request's first `q` at the target width, which does not fit the draft-width carrier, so the alternative is a failure on the first request.
- Initialize `draft_probs_list = None` outside the rejection-sampling branch, since the new call sites would otherwise raise `NameError` when rejection sampling is off.

`eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py` - size the decode graph's `draft_probs` input buffer by `draft_probs_vocab_size`, falling back to the model's vocab size for workers without it. Sized for the target vocabulary, capture fails on the first `torch.stack` and replay fails on `copy_`.

`arg_groups/speculative_hook.py` - `_should_auto_enable_hip_rejection_sampling` carried the same FIXME in its docstring ("rejection sampling still cannot consume a reduced / hot draft vocab"). Updated to reflect that the scatter now exists. The conservative behavior is kept: ROCm still does not auto-enable rejection sampling for EAGLE3 or for an EAGLE run with a token map, because this path has not been validated on ROCm. Passing the flag explicitly works.

`docs/docs/advanced_features/speculative_decoding.mdx` - `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` had no row in the speculative parameter table. Added one: default `False`, the `--speculative-eagle-topk 1` requirement, reduced-vocabulary support and its PD-decode limitation, and the UNO incompatibility, each checked against the code. The Block verification section said the draft must produce a full target-vocabulary proposal distribution; it now says how a reduced-vocabulary EAGLE3 draft's distribution reaches the target vocabulary.

`test/registered/unit/spec/test_draft_probs_reduced_vocab.py` - CPU unit tests, registered on `base-a-test-cpu`. Seven cover the scatter: hot columns land on their target ids, non-hot mass is exactly zero, total mass preserved, output is fp32 for any input dtype, no buffer aliasing across calls, width satisfies the `eagle_utils` guard, and a 400K-sample Monte Carlo showing chain rejection sampling with a truncated `q` reproduces `p` (max deviation within 4 standard errors). Two cover the assert: CUDA-graph filler rows pass, and a proposed token without mass fires.

`test/registered/e2e/speculative/test_eagle3_reject_sampling_reduced_vocab.py` - Llama-3.1-8B with its 32000-token EAGLE3 draft under `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` and `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT`, with overlap scheduling and CUDA graphs on. `SpecCorrectnessKit` covers startup (both graph variants are captured), greedy requests and one sampled request; `test_sampled_batch` sends nine sampled requests so the decode batch pads to the next captured size.

## Accuracy Tests

See the G-test result above, measured on the older fork described under "Where these numbers come from".

Local checks on this branch, CPU only: the 9 unit tests above pass, and 11 other CPU unit-test files that import the changed modules (162 tests, including `test_eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py` and `test_pd_eagle_draft_proposal.py`) pass the same before and after the change.

GPU check on one 80 GB Hopper GPU (SM 9.0), with torch 2.14.1+cu130 and the `pyproject.toml` dependencies but without `flashinfer-cubin`: the 9 unit tests pass, and the new e2e test passes all 5 cases (accept length 2.04 in `test_acc_length` and 1.45 in `test_batch_generation`; `test_sampled_batch` passes), with every CUDA graph captured under `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT`. On this PR's previous head (86d49be9a), which lacked the graph-buffer change, the same test fails at draft decode CUDA graph capture: `stack expects each tensor to be equal size, but got [64, 128256] at entry 0 and [64, 32000] at entry 1`. The run used an ungated copy of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and a 1800 s server launch timeout, because without the cubin package the first launch JIT-compiles kernels.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The added work is a single `index_copy_` per verify step on a `(bs, num_steps, target_vocab)` tensor. This path was previously unreachable for reduced-vocab drafts, so there is no prior behavior to regress.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

**Additional motivation: upstream now reaches this error without the flag**

Since this PR branched, `--speculative-use-block-verification` landed, and `handle_speculative_decoding` auto-enables rejection sampling for the EAGLE family:

```python
if (
    cfg.speculative_algorithm in ("EAGLE", "EAGLE3")
    and not cfg.speculative_use_rejection_sampling
):
    declare_resolution(
        server_args,
        "handle_speculative_decoding",
        speculative_use_rejection_sampling=True,
    )
```

So an EAGLE3 draft with a reduced (hot) vocabulary -- e.g. `draft_vocab_size=32000` against `target_vocab_size=128256` -- now hits the `ValueError` this PR removes without the user ever passing `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling`: enabling block verification is enough. What used to be an opt-in limitation is now a hard failure on a supported flag combination.

**Rebased** onto current main and force-pushed. The only conflict was in `eagle_worker_v2.py`, against the new all-greedy `needs_draft_probs` skip. The resolution keeps that gate and changes `_build_verify_draft_probs` to return early when `draft_probs_list is None`, which now covers both "rejection sampling off" and "all-greedy batch verified by argmax" -- the guard this PR originally shipped would have called `torch.stack(None)` on an all-greedy batch. `ruff`, `ruff-format` and `isort` are clean, and the 7 unit tests in `test/registered/unit/spec/test_draft_probs_reduced_vocab.py` still pass.

**CI**: no test has actually run on this PR yet. `pr-gate` fails at the `Require run-ci label` step, so every downstream job is skipped and the red checks are all aggregation jobs rather than real failures. I can't add the label myself -- I'm not in `.github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json`, so `can_tag_run_ci_label` is false and the tag-and-rerun slash command only performs the rerun half for me. Could a maintainer add `run-ci`?

<!-- mintlify-fork-preview-approval -->
### Preview approval required

This pull request comes from a fork, so Mintlify won't build a preview until someone with write access approves commit `7c844fe`.

[Approve preview](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40893/checks?check_run_id=126292368830)

Rebased onto current main (`e33cd0c`). Still 1 commit / 5 files, no conflicts, and the patch is unchanged from the previous head (identical `git patch-id`). I also fixed the commit author, which the previous push carried from a misconfigured local identity, and retitled the PR for the new title check. `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes (isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1, ruff-format, codespell, and the registered-test checks).

The `ValueError` this PR removes is still on main:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e33cd0c3a10474c7a0f6efeb69ce2cf4b7a55021/python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py#L264-L278

and it is now reachable without passing `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling`. With `--speculative-use-block-verification`, `handle_speculative_decoding` turns rejection sampling on for EAGLE / EAGLE3:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e33cd0c3a10474c7a0f6efeb69ce2cf4b7a55021/python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/speculative_hook.py#L178-L198

So an EAGLE3 draft with a reduced hot vocab fails at startup whenever block verification is on.

@ch-wan, could you add `run-ci` and take a look? No test has run on this PR yet: `pr-gate` stops at `Require run-ci label`, and I am not in `.github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json`.

Thanks for this. The description says the PR's code had not been run end to end yet, so we tried it on one H100 80GB with a public reduced-vocab pair.

**Setup**
- Target `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` (vocab 151,936). EAGLE3 draft `Tengyunw/qwen3_30b_moe_eagle3` (`draft_vocab_size` 32,000, with a d2t map). TP1.
- Image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261103-797af717`, with the source replaced by main `8d4e1ce4c7`, or by this PR's head `02657ab39c` merged onto it (no conflicts). Both arms ran on the same node.
- Server:
  ```
  python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --tp 1 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
    --max-running-requests 64 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE3 \
    --speculative-draft-model-path Tengyunw/qwen3_30b_moe_eagle3 \
    --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
    [--speculative-use-rejection-sampling]
  ```

**Results**
- main with `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` refuses to start with the `draft vocab (32000) != target vocab (151936)` ValueError. With this PR it starts with CUDA graphs on and served every request without errors. `test_draft_probs_reduced_vocab.py` passes (9/9) on H100.
- Acceptance length (total completion tokens / total verify steps). The workload is 64 prompts × 256 new tokens, 16 concurrent, with a fixed `sampling_seed` per request:

  | arm | T=1.0 | T=0.6 | T=0.6 output tok/s |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | main, no flag (target-only verify) | 1.658 | 1.743 | 1258 |
  | this PR, no flag (target-only verify) | 1.676 | 1.766 | 1247 |
  | this PR, `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` | 1.585 | 1.695 | 1215 |

  On this pair, rejection sampling accepts about 4–5% fewer tokens than the target-only verifier. That runs the other way from the +26% in the description, which came from a different model pair. So the gain seems to depend on how well the draft's q is calibrated, and it may be worth softening that claim in the docs.
- Distribution check, following your G-test design: 6 prompts × 3,000 samples, T=1, top-p 1, top-k -1, 2nd–4th generated tokens. Tokens with fewer than 20 pooled samples were merged into one cell; at this N the unbinned test flags even two plain launches as different.

  | pair | G/df | p |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | no-spec launch A vs launch B (floor) | 1.06 | 0.14 |
  | A vs this PR, rejection sampling | 1.17 | 0.002 |
  | B vs this PR, rejection sampling | 1.24 | 2e-5 |
  | A vs target-only verify | 1.15 | 0.005 |
  | B vs target-only verify | 1.23 | 5e-5 |

  Both speculative arms sit about the same distance above the cross-launch floor. At this sample size we see no difference between the new rejection-sampling path and the existing path. The test is not powered to resolve a small bias either way.

Raw logs and scripts are available if useful.

Thanks for testing this on a public pair, and for following the G-test design.

Agreed, +26% was too strong as a general claim. Rejection sampling only beats the target-only verifier when the draft's `q` overlaps the target well, and the gain shrinks on low-entropy text. I've updated the description with what we measured: three internal draft/target pairs, each with 7 draft steps, gained +13% to +33% on average and +3% to +46% per benchmark, and the lowest-entropy sets (humaneval, mbpp) gained least in every pair. Your pair differs on all three things that moved it for us: the entropy of the workload, the strength of the draft (accept length about 1.7 with 3 steps), and the number of draft steps. Could you share which 64 prompts you used?

The docs row doesn't claim a speedup: it says a reduced-vocabulary draft is supported, with lower acceptance and an unchanged output distribution.

On the distribution check, agreed that 6 prompts × 3,000 samples can't separate the two speculative paths. Ours used 8 prompts × 10,000 samples (20,000 for the reference) at T=1, pooled over positions 2-4, with a second independent non-speculative launch as the floor. At that size the target-only path sat 21% above the floor (pooled p = 3.2e-26) and the new path sat on it.

Following up on the evidence I posted earlier: here is an optional follow-up on top of this PR, in case you'd like to fold it in.

Branch: https://github.com/esarafian/sglang/commits/reduced-vocab-mapped-draft-q (4 commits directly on your current head `7c844fe`; they cherry-pick cleanly).

**What it does:** with a reduced draft vocabulary, `q` currently gets scattered into a zero-filled `(bs, steps, target_vocab)` FP32 tensor at the verify boundary. With this change, `chain_speculative_sampling_triton` reads the compact draft-width `q` through a target→draft index map instead. The map comes from `hot_token_id` / `d2t`, the kernel uses a `MAPPED_Q` constexpr path, and the result is the same FP32 value for every target id, with 0.0 outside the draft vocabulary. Tile size and reduction order are unchanged, so outputs are bitwise identical. NPU keeps the scatter.

**Verify step** (3 draft steps, 32K draft vocab, CUDA graph, cold L2), scatter + verify → mapped verify:
| target vocab, bs | RTX PRO 6000 | GB200 | H100 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 151,936, bs 64 | 313 → 119 µs (2.6×) | 275 → 113 µs (2.4×) | 462 → 110 µs (4.2×) |
| 151,936, bs 128 | 758 → 139 µs (5.5×) | 425 → 122 µs (3.5×) | 821 → 124 µs (6.6×) |
| 248,320, bs 128 | 1675 → 206 µs (8.1×) | 608 → 194 µs (3.1×) | 1038 → 201 µs (5.2×) |

Small batches are about equal; H100 at bs 1 with a 248K vocab is 4-8 µs slower. End-to-end serving with Qwen3-30B-A3B + EAGLE3 is unchanged within noise, because the forward pass dominates there.

**Tests:**
- new `test_reject_sampling_mapped_draft_q.py`: mapped vs scattered `q`, bitwise-equal predicts, accept index and lengths; token-wise and block verification; vocabs 17 to 248K, including NaN/inf/subnormal `q`;
- the existing `test_draft_probs_reduced_vocab.py` is extended;
- one existing test fake gains `target_to_draft_vocab=None`.

Deterministic end-to-end runs vs this PR are token-identical apart from one request that also varies between base launches.

Happy to open it as a separate PR after this one merges instead, if you prefer.

Thanks for putting this together, and for the careful bitwise-equality tests. The verify-step numbers at large batch sizes are a nice win.

Since it changes `chain_speculative_sampling_triton`, I'd prefer to keep it out of this PR so the kernel change gets its own review. Please open it as a separate PR once this one merges.

- On a PD-disaggregation decode server, reject a reduced draft vocabulary under rejection sampling at startup. `pd_first_draft_proposal` builds a request's first `q` at the target width, which does not fit the draft-width carrier, so the alternative is a failure on the first request.
- Initialize `draft_probs_list = None` outside the rejection-sampling branch, since the new call sites would otherwise raise `NameError` when rejection sampling is off.

`eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py` - size the decode graph's `draft_probs` input buffer by `draft_probs_vocab_size`, falling back to the model's vocab size for workers without it. Sized for the target vocabulary, capture fails on the first `torch.stack` and replay fails on `copy_`.

`arg_groups/speculative_hook.py` - `_should_auto_enable_hip_rejection_sampling` carried the same FIXME in its docstring ("rejection sampling still cannot consume a reduced / hot draft vocab"). Updated to reflect that the scatter now exists. The conservative behavior is kept: ROCm still does not auto-enable rejection sampling for EAGLE3 or for an EAGLE run with a token map, because this path has not been validated on ROCm. Passing the flag explicitly works.

`docs/docs/advanced_features/speculative_decoding.mdx` - `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` had no row in the speculative parameter table. Added one: default `False`, the `--speculative-eagle-topk 1` requirement, reduced-vocabulary support and its PD-decode limitation, and the UNO incompatibility, each checked against the code. The Block verification section said the draft must produce a full target-vocabulary proposal distribution; it now says how a reduced-vocabulary EAGLE3 draft's distribution reaches the target vocabulary.

`test/registered/unit/spec/test_draft_probs_reduced_vocab.py` - CPU unit tests, registered on `base-a-test-cpu`. Seven cover the scatter: hot columns land on their target ids, non-hot mass is exactly zero, total mass preserved, output is fp32 for any input dtype, no buffer aliasing across calls, width satisfies the `eagle_utils` guard, and a 400K-sample Monte Carlo showing chain rejection sampling with a truncated `q` reproduces `p` (max deviation within 4 standard errors). Two cover the assert: CUDA-graph filler rows pass, and a proposed token without mass fires.

`test/registered/e2e/speculative/test_eagle3_reject_sampling_reduced_vocab.py` - Llama-3.1-8B with its 32000-token EAGLE3 draft under `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` and `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT`, with overlap scheduling and CUDA graphs on. `SpecCorrectnessKit` covers startup (both graph variants are captured), greedy requests and one sampled request; `test_sampled_batch` sends nine sampled requests so the decode batch pads to the next captured size.

## Accuracy Tests

See the G-test result above, measured on the older fork described under "Where these numbers come from".

Local checks on this branch, CPU only: the 9 unit tests above pass, and 11 other CPU unit-test files that import the changed modules (162 tests, including `test_eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py` and `test_pd_eagle_draft_proposal.py`) pass the same before and after the change.

GPU check on one 80 GB Hopper GPU (SM 9.0), with torch 2.14.1+cu130 and the `pyproject.toml` dependencies but without `flashinfer-cubin`: the 9 unit tests pass, and the new e2e test passes all 5 cases (accept length 2.04 in `test_acc_length` and 1.45 in `test_batch_generation`; `test_sampled_batch` passes), with every CUDA graph captured under `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT`. On this PR's previous head (86d49be9a), which lacked the graph-buffer change, the same test fails at draft decode CUDA graph capture: `stack expects each tensor to be equal size, but got [64, 128256] at entry 0 and [64, 32000] at entry 1`. The run used an ungated copy of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and a 1800 s server launch timeout, because without the cubin package the first launch JIT-compiles kernels.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The added work is a single `index_copy_` per verify step on a `(bs, num_steps, target_vocab)` tensor. This path was previously unreachable for reduced-vocab drafts, so there is no prior behavior to regress.

+"""EAGLE3 rejection sampling with a reduced (hot) draft vocabulary.
+
+The Llama-3.1 EAGLE3 draft emits 32000 logits against a 128256-token target.
+Rejection sampling carries each step's q at the draft width, through the decode
+CUDA graph and the overlap future map, and scatters it onto the target
+vocabulary through the d2t map only at verify. A q buffer sized for the target
+vocabulary fails graph capture on its first torch.stack.
+
+SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT turns a misaligned scatter (q == 0 on a proposed
+token) into a crash instead of an inflated accept length. Greedy requests verify
+by argmax and never build q, so test_sampled_batch sends sampled requests, nine
+of them so the decode batch pads to the next captured size.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+import requests
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.kits.spec_server_kits import SpecCorrectnessKit
+from sglang.test.server_fixtures.spec_eagle_fixture import Eagle3Base
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=150, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+
+class TestEagle3RejectSamplingReducedVocab(Eagle3Base, SpecCorrectnessKit):
+    extra_args = ("--speculative-use-rejection-sampling",)
+    env_overrides = ((envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT, True),)
+
+    def test_sampled_batch(self):
+        prompts = [f"Write a short story about the number {i}." for i in range(9)]
+        results = requests.post(
+            self.base_url + "/generate",
+            json={
+                "text": prompts,
+                "sampling_params": {"temperature": 1.0, "max_new_tokens": 64},
+            },
+        ).json()
+        total_completion, total_verify = 0, 0
+        for r in results:
+            self.assertIn("text", r, f"Server error: {r}")
+            total_completion += r["meta_info"]["completion_tokens"]
+            total_verify += r["meta_info"].get("spec_verify_ct", 0)
+        self.assertGreater(total_verify, 0)
+        # A q supported only on the hot set lowers acceptance but keeps drafts
+        # acceptable.
+        self.assertGreater(total_completion / total_verify, 1.0)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

@@ -0,0 +1,157 @@
+"""Unit tests for EAGLE3 rejection sampling with a reduced (hot) draft vocabulary.
+
+The draft head emits ``draft_vocab_size`` columns and ``hot_token_id`` maps them
+onto target token ids, so ``q`` has to be lifted to the target vocabulary before
+the chain kernel -- which indexes ``q`` by target token id -- can read it.
+``eagle_utils`` rejects a ``draft_probs`` whose last dim does not match
+``target_probs``, so the width contract is what these tests pin down.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.speculative.eagle_worker_v2 import EagleDraftWorker
+from sglang.srt.speculative.spec_utils import scatter_draft_probs_to_target_vocab
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestScatterDraftProbsToTargetVocab(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.target_vocab = 16
+        self.hot_token_id = torch.tensor([1, 3, 4, 9, 15], dtype=torch.int64)
+        self.draft_vocab = self.hot_token_id.numel()
+
+    def test_hot_columns_land_on_their_target_ids(self):
+        draft_probs = torch.rand(2, 3, self.draft_vocab)
+        draft_probs /= draft_probs.sum(-1, keepdim=True)
+
+        out = scatter_draft_probs_to_target_vocab(
+            draft_probs, self.hot_token_id, self.target_vocab
+        )
+
+        self.assertEqual(out.shape, (2, 3, self.target_vocab))
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out[..., self.hot_token_id], draft_probs)
+
+    def test_non_hot_mass_is_exactly_zero(self):
+        # q(x) = 0 off the hot set is the true proposal mass, not an
+        # approximation: the draft can only ever propose a hot token. That is
+        # what lets relu(p - q) keep the full p on non-hot tokens.
+        draft_probs = torch.rand(4, 2, self.draft_vocab)
+        out = scatter_draft_probs_to_target_vocab(
+            draft_probs, self.hot_token_id, self.target_vocab
+        )
+
+        cold = torch.ones(self.target_vocab, dtype=torch.bool)
+        cold[self.hot_token_id] = False
+        self.assertEqual(out[..., cold].count_nonzero().item(), 0)
+
+    def test_total_mass_is_preserved(self):
+        draft_probs = torch.rand(3, 5, self.draft_vocab)
+        draft_probs /= draft_probs.sum(-1, keepdim=True)
+        out = scatter_draft_probs_to_target_vocab(
+            draft_probs, self.hot_token_id, self.target_vocab
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out.sum(-1), torch.ones(3, 5), rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-6)
+
+    def test_output_is_fp32_for_any_input_dtype(self):
+        # The eager and CUDA-graph paths must hand the kernel the same dtype,
+        # so the output dtype is pinned rather than inherited from the input.
+        for dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32):
+            out = scatter_draft_probs_to_target_vocab(
+                torch.rand(2, 1, self.draft_vocab, dtype=dtype),
+                self.hot_token_id,
+                self.target_vocab,
+            )
+            self.assertEqual(out.dtype, torch.float32, msg=f"input dtype {dtype}")
+
+    def test_no_buffer_reuse_across_calls(self):
+        # The returned tensor outlives the call under overlap scheduling, so a
+        # cached buffer would alias across iterations.
+        a = scatter_draft_probs_to_target_vocab(
+            torch.zeros(1, 1, self.draft_vocab), self.hot_token_id, self.target_vocab
+        )
+        b = scatter_draft_probs_to_target_vocab(
+            torch.ones(1, 1, self.draft_vocab), self.hot_token_id, self.target_vocab
+        )
+        self.assertNotEqual(a.data_ptr(), b.data_ptr())
+        self.assertEqual(a.count_nonzero().item(), 0)
+
+    def test_width_matches_target_probs_contract(self):
+        # eagle_utils raises when draft_probs.shape[-1] != target_probs.shape[-1].
+        target_probs = torch.rand(2, 3, self.target_vocab)
+        out = scatter_draft_probs_to_target_vocab(
+            torch.rand(2, 3, self.draft_vocab), self.hot_token_id, self.target_vocab
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(out.shape[-1], target_probs.shape[-1])
+
+    def test_chain_rejection_sampling_stays_unbiased(self):
+        """A truncated q does not bias the sampler, it only lowers acceptance.
+
+        Monte-Carlo the accept test the chain kernel runs -- accept with
+        ``min(1, p/q)``, otherwise resample from ``relu(p - q)`` -- with q
+        supported only on the hot set, and check the emitted distribution is p.
+        """
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        n = 400_000
+        p = torch.rand(self.target_vocab)
+        p /= p.sum()
+        hot_q = torch.rand(self.draft_vocab)
+        hot_q /= hot_q.sum()
+        q = scatter_draft_probs_to_target_vocab(
+            hot_q.view(1, 1, -1), self.hot_token_id, self.target_vocab
+        ).view(-1)
+
+        proposed = self.hot_token_id[torch.multinomial(hot_q, n, replacement=True)]
+        accepted = torch.rand(n) < (p[proposed] / q[proposed]).clamp(max=1.0)
+
+        counts = torch.zeros(self.target_vocab)
+        counts.index_add_(0, proposed[accepted], torch.ones(int(accepted.sum())))
+        residual = (p - q).clamp(min=0)
+        residual /= residual.sum()
+        n_rejected = int((~accepted).sum())
+        counts.index_add_(
+            0,
+            torch.multinomial(residual, n_rejected, replacement=True),
+            torch.ones(n_rejected),
+        )
+
+        empirical = counts / n
+        standard_error = (p * (1 - p) / n).sqrt().max()
+        self.assertLess(float((empirical - p).abs().max()), 4 * float(standard_error))
+
+
+class TestVerifyDraftProbsAssert(CustomTestCase):
+    """The ``q > 0`` probe in ``_build_verify_draft_probs`` under async asserts."""
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.worker = object.__new__(EagleDraftWorker)
+        self.worker.hot_token_id = torch.tensor([1, 3, 4, 9, 15], dtype=torch.int64)
+        self.worker.target_vocab_size = 16
+        # Two requests, three chain slots; slot i's token is drawn from row i.
+        self.rows = [torch.full((2, 5), 0.2) for _ in range(3)]
+        self.draft_tokens = self.worker.hot_token_id[
+            torch.tensor([[0, 2, 4], [1, 3, 0]])
+        ]
+
+    def test_cuda_graph_filler_rows_pass(self):
+        # Capture warms up on the zeroed q buffer and replay zeroes padded rows.
+        self.rows[0][1] = 0
+        with envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT.override(True):
+            out = self.worker._build_verify_draft_probs(self.rows, self.draft_tokens)
+        self.assertEqual(out.shape, (2, 3, 16))
+
+    def test_proposed_token_without_mass_fires(self):
+        # Target id 2 is not hot, so its scattered q is 0 although the row has mass.
+        self.draft_tokens[0, 1] = 2
+        with envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT.override(True):
+            with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
+                self.worker._build_verify_draft_probs(self.rows, self.draft_tokens)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

issue_comments.body:
**Additional motivation: upstream now reaches this error without the flag**

Since this PR branched, `--speculative-use-block-verification` landed, and `handle_speculative_decoding` auto-enables rejection sampling for the EAGLE family:

```python
if (
    cfg.speculative_algorithm in ("EAGLE", "EAGLE3")
    and not cfg.speculative_use_rejection_sampling
):
    declare_resolution(
        server_args,
        "handle_speculative_decoding",
        speculative_use_rejection_sampling=True,
    )
```

So an EAGLE3 draft with a reduced (hot) vocabulary -- e.g. `draft_vocab_size=32000` against `target_vocab_size=128256` -- now hits the `ValueError` this PR removes without the user ever passing `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling`: enabling block verification is enough. What used to be an opt-in limitation is now a hard failure on a supported flag combination.

**Rebased** onto current main and force-pushed. The only conflict was in `eagle_worker_v2.py`, against the new all-greedy `needs_draft_probs` skip. The resolution keeps that gate and changes `_build_verify_draft_probs` to return early when `draft_probs_list is None`, which now covers both "rejection sampling off" and "all-greedy batch verified by argmax" -- the guard this PR originally shipped would have called `torch.stack(None)` on an all-greedy batch. `ruff`, `ruff-format` and `isort` are clean, and the 7 unit tests in `test/registered/unit/spec/test_draft_probs_reduced_vocab.py` still pass.

**CI**: no test has actually run on this PR yet. `pr-gate` fails at the `Require run-ci label` step, so every downstream job is skipped and the red checks are all aggregation jobs rather than real failures. I can't add the label myself -- I'm not in `.github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json`, so `can_tag_run_ci_label` is false and the tag-and-rerun slash command only performs the rerun half for me. Could a maintainer add `run-ci`?

Thanks for this. The description says the PR's code had not been run end to end yet, so we tried it on one H100 80GB with a public reduced-vocab pair.

**Setup**
- Target `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` (vocab 151,936). EAGLE3 draft `Tengyunw/qwen3_30b_moe_eagle3` (`draft_vocab_size` 32,000, with a d2t map). TP1.
- Image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261103-797af717`, with the source replaced by main `8d4e1ce4c7`, or by this PR's head `02657ab39c` merged onto it (no conflicts). Both arms ran on the same node.
- Server:
  ```
  python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --tp 1 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
    --max-running-requests 64 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE3 \
    --speculative-draft-model-path Tengyunw/qwen3_30b_moe_eagle3 \
    --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
    [--speculative-use-rejection-sampling]
  ```

**Results**
- main with `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` refuses to start with the `draft vocab (32000) != target vocab (151936)` ValueError. With this PR it starts with CUDA graphs on and served every request without errors. `test_draft_probs_reduced_vocab.py` passes (9/9) on H100.
- Acceptance length (total completion tokens / total verify steps). The workload is 64 prompts × 256 new tokens, 16 concurrent, with a fixed `sampling_seed` per request:

  | arm | T=1.0 | T=0.6 | T=0.6 output tok/s |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | main, no flag (target-only verify) | 1.658 | 1.743 | 1258 |
  | this PR, no flag (target-only verify) | 1.676 | 1.766 | 1247 |
  | this PR, `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` | 1.585 | 1.695 | 1215 |

  On this pair, rejection sampling accepts about 4–5% fewer tokens than the target-only verifier. That runs the other way from the +26% in the description, which came from a different model pair. So the gain seems to depend on how well the draft's q is calibrated, and it may be worth softening that claim in the docs.
- Distribution check, following your G-test design: 6 prompts × 3,000 samples, T=1, top-p 1, top-k -1, 2nd–4th generated tokens. Tokens with fewer than 20 pooled samples were merged into one cell; at this N the unbinned test flags even two plain launches as different.

  | pair | G/df | p |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | no-spec launch A vs launch B (floor) | 1.06 | 0.14 |
  | A vs this PR, rejection sampling | 1.17 | 0.002 |
  | B vs this PR, rejection sampling | 1.24 | 2e-5 |
  | A vs target-only verify | 1.15 | 0.005 |
  | B vs target-only verify | 1.23 | 5e-5 |

  Both speculative arms sit about the same distance above the cross-launch floor. At this sample size we see no difference between the new rejection-sampling path and the existing path. The test is not powered to resolve a small bias either way.

Raw logs and scripts are available if useful.

Thanks for testing this on a public pair, and for following the G-test design.

Agreed, +26% was too strong as a general claim. Rejection sampling only beats the target-only verifier when the draft's `q` overlaps the target well, and the gain shrinks on low-entropy text. I've updated the description with what we measured: three internal draft/target pairs, each with 7 draft steps, gained +13% to +33% on average and +3% to +46% per benchmark, and the lowest-entropy sets (humaneval, mbpp) gained least in every pair. Your pair differs on all three things that moved it for us: the entropy of the workload, the strength of the draft (accept length about 1.7 with 3 steps), and the number of draft steps. Could you share which 64 prompts you used?

The docs row doesn't claim a speedup: it says a reduced-vocabulary draft is supported, with lower acceptance and an unchanged output distribution.

On the distribution check, agreed that 6 prompts × 3,000 samples can't separate the two speculative paths. Ours used 8 prompts × 10,000 samples (20,000 for the reference) at T=1, pooled over positions 2-4, with a second independent non-speculative launch as the floor. At that size the target-only path sat 21% above the floor (pooled p = 3.2e-26) and the new path sat on it.

Following up on the evidence I posted earlier: here is an optional follow-up on top of this PR, in case you'd like to fold it in.

Branch: https://github.com/esarafian/sglang/commits/reduced-vocab-mapped-draft-q (4 commits directly on your current head `7c844fe`; they cherry-pick cleanly).

**What it does:** with a reduced draft vocabulary, `q` currently gets scattered into a zero-filled `(bs, steps, target_vocab)` FP32 tensor at the verify boundary. With this change, `chain_speculative_sampling_triton` reads the compact draft-width `q` through a target→draft index map instead. The map comes from `hot_token_id` / `d2t`, the kernel uses a `MAPPED_Q` constexpr path, and the result is the same FP32 value for every target id, with 0.0 outside the draft vocabulary. Tile size and reduction order are unchanged, so outputs are bitwise identical. NPU keeps the scatter.

**Verify step** (3 draft steps, 32K draft vocab, CUDA graph, cold L2), scatter + verify → mapped verify:
| target vocab, bs | RTX PRO 6000 | GB200 | H100 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 151,936, bs 64 | 313 → 119 µs (2.6×) | 275 → 113 µs (2.4×) | 462 → 110 µs (4.2×) |
| 151,936, bs 128 | 758 → 139 µs (5.5×) | 425 → 122 µs (3.5×) | 821 → 124 µs (6.6×) |
| 248,320, bs 128 | 1675 → 206 µs (8.1×) | 608 → 194 µs (3.1×) | 1038 → 201 µs (5.2×) |

Small batches are about equal; H100 at bs 1 with a 248K vocab is 4-8 µs slower. End-to-end serving with Qwen3-30B-A3B + EAGLE3 is unchanged within noise, because the forward pass dominates there.

**Tests:**
- new `test_reject_sampling_mapped_draft_q.py`: mapped vs scattered `q`, bitwise-equal predicts, accept index and lengths; token-wise and block verification; vocabs 17 to 248K, including NaN/inf/subnormal `q`;
- the existing `test_draft_probs_reduced_vocab.py` is extended;
- one existing test fake gains `target_to_draft_vocab=None`.

Deterministic end-to-end runs vs this PR are token-identical apart from one request that also varies between base launches.

Happy to open it as a separate PR after this one merges instead, if you prefer.

Thanks for putting this together, and for the careful bitwise-equality tests. The verify-step numbers at large batch sizes are a nice win.

Since it changes `chain_speculative_sampling_triton`, I'd prefer to keep it out of this PR so the kernel change gets its own review. Please open it as a separate PR once this one merges.
